skill.name: enrich-from-linkedin
skill.description: Use Leadsets to look up current roles, companies, and work email status from one or more LinkedIn profile URLs. The skill checks quotas and separates verified addresses from uncertain results.
skill.summary: Turn LinkedIn profile URLs into contact records with role, company, and work email status from Leadsets.
skill.author: leadsets

security_audit.summary: The shell, environment access, and reconnaissance alerts are documentation or workflow text, not evidence of those behaviors. The documented Leadsets lookup sends LinkedIn profile URLs to an external service, and exports lack explicit checks on destination access. No evidence found of prompt injection or credential exfiltration.

remediation.issue: Profile URLs are sent to Leadsets during enrichment.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose the external transfer before sending the first profile and confirm that the user is authorized to share the URLs.

remediation.issue: Contact exports can expose names, work emails, and employment data to unintended recipients.
remediation.suggestion: Confirm the export destination and intended recipients. Check sharing settings before writing to Google Sheets, and do not export to public destinations.

content.value_statement: A LinkedIn profile link may not give you a current job title or a reliable work email. Use Leadsets to fill those gaps and see which addresses it could verify.
actual_capabilities: Accepts personal LinkedIn profile URLs from chat, a CSV column, or a connected Google Sheet.
Removes tracking parameters, trailing slashes, and duplicate URLs. Reports links that are not personal profiles.
Checks the Leadsets allowance and tests one profile before processing a batch.
Returns available job titles, company names and domains, work emails, verification statuses, confidence, and check dates.
Flags employer changes when the input includes a company name.
Separates results by email status and provides counts in chat, CSV, or a connected Google Sheet.
limitations: Requires a Leadsets account and a configured MCP connection or REST API key.
Does not scrape LinkedIn or retrieve content behind a login. It relies on Leadsets data.
Does not guess missing email addresses or provide phone numbers. Some profiles are not found or have no verified address.
Batch size depends on the remaining allowance. Google Sheets output requires an existing connection.

prompt_templates.title: Check one profile
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Leadsets to check [LinkedIn profile URL]. Show the role, company, and work email status in chat.
prompt_templates.scenario: One profile you are authorized to share with Leadsets.

prompt_templates.title: Review a short list
prompt_templates.prompt: Enrich [profile URL list]. Report the unique profile count and any rejected links. Keep catch-all and unknown results separate from verified addresses.
prompt_templates.scenario: An approved list of personal profiles.

prompt_templates.title: Compare employers
prompt_templates.prompt: Enrich up to 25 profiles from [CSV] after checking the Leadsets allowance. Compare results with [company column] and flag employer changes in chat.
prompt_templates.scenario: A CSV with LinkedIn URLs and recorded employers.

prompt_templates.title: Export a quota-limited batch
prompt_templates.prompt: Check usage before enriching [LinkedIn URL column] from [approved sheet]. Test one profile and cap the run at 100. Write results to [approved private sheet] and report any URLs left.
prompt_templates.scenario: A managed batch with an approved export destination.

output_examples.input: Enrich five unique profiles from a private CSV.
output: Three profiles were enriched and one was not found.
The three contacts had two verified addresses and one missing address.
One profile remains because the enrichment allowance was reached.

best_practices: Confirm that you can share each profile URL with Leadsets before starting.
Set a batch cap and review the test record before processing the rest.
Use a private export destination and check who can access it.
anti_patterns: Treating catch-all or unknown addresses as verified.
Submitting company pages, posts, or LinkedIn search URLs as personal profiles.
Exporting enriched records to a public sheet or a folder with unnecessary access.

faq.question: What do I need to connect?
faq.answer: You need a Leadsets account and access through the Leadsets MCP server or a REST API key.

faq.question: Does it scrape LinkedIn?
faq.answer: No. It sends the profile URL to Leadsets and uses that service's data.

faq.question: What does catch-all mean?
faq.answer: The domain accepts mail for many addresses, so Leadsets cannot confirm that the individual mailbox exists.

faq.question: What can count against my allowance?
faq.answer: A profile returned with data uses one enrichment record. A not-found result uses a request but no enrichment record.

faq.question: What happens when the allowance runs out?
faq.answer: The skill stops when no allowance remains and reports what is left. It includes reset timing when Leadsets provides it.

faq.question: Where can I get the results?
faq.answer: Small runs default to a chat table. Larger runs default to CSV, and Google Sheets requires a connected account.
